# QS-CFW-3043-62 Quality specification - flange blank CFW-3043-62 (4140) Rev D

Plant: P1  
Part: CFW-3043-62

Scope
This quality specification defines the metallurgical and dimensional acceptance criteria, inspection methods, and nonconformance handling for flange blank CFW-3043-62 produced from 4140 material at Plant P1. It is intended for use by forging, heat treat, machining, quality, and shipping personnel to ensure consistent part quality and traceability through production. Background rationale is provided to explain why each requirement is controlled and how inspection records shall be maintained. This document applies to all production lots of flange blank CFW-3043-62 and to material received for processing that will be converted to that part.

Requirements table
The table below lists the controlled characteristics, the acceptance criteria, and the required record to be retained with the lot traveler.

| Characteristic | Acceptance criterion | Record to retain |
|---|---:|---|
| Material grade | 4140 per purchase specification | Mill certificate attached to lot traveler |
| Hardness (through-thickness, final condition) | The hardness range for flange blank CFW-3043-62 (CFW-3043-62) is 37-43 HRC. | Hardness test report with location map |
| Bore diameter tolerance (as-formed) | The bore diameter tolerance for flange blank CFW-3043-62 (CFW-3043-62) is ±0.04 mm. | Dimensional inspection report showing measured bore and nominal |
| Maximum forging weight | The maximum forging weight for flange blank CFW-3043-62 (CFW-3043-62) is 28.1 kg. | Forging log with actual gross and net weights recorded |
| Surface condition | Free from forge laps, cold shuts, and cracks that penetrate inspection acceptance depth | Visual inspection report |
| Traceability | Each blank must be marked with lot identifier and included on traveler | Marking record and traveler |

Inspection method
Hardness
- Take hardness measurements on each representative blank following a defined sampling plan. Measure at locations that represent critical section changes and the bore ID; provide a location map on the report. Use a calibrated Rockwell hardness tester set to the appropriate scale and technique for through-thickness evaluation. Report individual readings and the location map; record any outlier and its disposition. The hardness data shall be filed with the lot documentation.
- Rationale: Hardness controls are used to confirm heat treatment and material condition; the specified hardness range reduces risk of premature wear or excessive brittleness while preserving toughness for subsequent machining and service.

Dimensional inspection
- Verify the bore diameter at the specified critical plane(s) using a calibrated bore gauge or micrometric method that provides the resolution required to demonstrate compliance with the stated tolerance. Record the nominal dimension and the measured size for each inspected blank on the dimensional inspection report.
- Examples:
  - For a blank measured at the critical bore plane, list nominal, measured, and deviation. Indicate compliance when deviation is within the stated tolerance. Nonconforming bores shall be segregated and submitted for disposition.
- Rationale: Tight bore control minimizes rework and ensures fitment in assembly. The bore tolerance is set to accommodate downstream machining allowances and to control concentricity requirements.

Weight control
- Record forging weight for each blank immediately after the primary forging operation. Compare the recorded weight to the maximum forging weight specified. Blanks exceeding the maximum forging weight shall be quarantined for review.
- Rationale: Maximum forging weight is controlled to ensure die life, press capacity, and handling safety; it also identifies potential material or process deviations.

Surface and visual inspection
- Perform visual and tactile inspection under adequate lighting for surface defects. Mark and document areas of concern on the part sketch. Small, non-penetrating surface irregularities may be eligible for repair by approved grinding procedures; deeper defects require engineering disposition.

Calibration and equipment
- All measurement instruments used for hardness, bore, and weight verification must be calibrated and traceable to national standards. Calibration records shall be available for audit.

Sampling and acceptance
- Sampling for destructive and nondestructive tests shall follow the plant’s sampling procedure. Acceptance is based on the requirements table. Material that meets all listed criteria shall be released with the lot traveler; material that fails any criterion shall follow the nonconformance handling procedure below.

Records to keep
- Mill certificate for material grade.  
- Hardness test report with location map and individual readings.  
- Dimensional inspection report showing nominal, measured, and deviation values for the bore.  
- Forging log showing recorded forging weight and operator initials.  
- Visual inspection report and marked part sketch for any surface findings.  
- Calibration certificates for instruments used.  
- Traveler indicating lot identifier and final disposition.

Nonconformance handling
Identification and segregation
- Any blank found outside the acceptance criteria in the requirements table shall be clearly identified, marked, and segregated from acceptable material. The lot traveler must be annotated to indicate the nonconforming status and the nature of the failure.

Disposition and review
- The quality engineer shall evaluate nonconforming blanks and propose one of the following dispositions: repair, rework, or scrap. Repair must follow an approved engineering repair instruction and be documented explicitly on the traveler. Rework that affects controlled dimensions or material condition requires reinspection to the original acceptance criteria prior to release.

Root cause and corrective action
- For any nonconformance, initiate a cause analysis to determine source of failure. Document containment and corrective action in the plant quality system records. Examples of typical corrective actions include adjustments to forging operation, maintenance on tooling, or changes in heat treat practice; all corrective actions must be validated to prevent recurrence.

Disposition records
- Maintain a complete record of nonconformance, investigation, disposition, and verification of corrective action with the lot documentation. Records shall include the nonconformance description, photos if applicable, calculated deviations, disposition decision, and signatures of the responsible personnel.

Review and release
- Final release of a lot to shipping requires closure of all nonconformance records and completion of required inspections listed in this document. The lot traveler, with attached test and inspection reports, shall be retained as the permanent record for traceability.
